Predisposition

pree-dis-puh-ZISH-un · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Predisposition is a tendency to think, feel, or act in a particular way, often due to nature or prior conditioning.

Researchers believe a predisposition toward anxiety can run in families, though environment plays a role too.

Worked Example

Having grown up sailing with her grandfather every summer, Maya seemed to have a natural predisposition toward a career on the water.

A predisposition is a leaning or tendency someone already has -- it doesn't guarantee an outcome, but it makes that outcome more likely.

How Predisposition Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

tendency

tendency: an inclination to act in a particular way

penchant

penchant: a strong natural liking or tendency

Antonyms

aversion

aversion: a strong dislike or disinclination

resistance

resistance: opposition to something

How Strong Is It? — leaning → propensity → predisposition

leaning vs. predisposition

leaning vs. predisposition: A leaning is a mild, casual tendency, without predisposition's stronger sense of something built in ahead of time.

propensity vs. predisposition

propensity vs. predisposition: Propensity describes a strong, almost inevitable-feeling tendency, more forceful than a simple predisposition.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — pre-

prefix — pre-: before (Latin)

root — disposition

root — disposition: a person's general nature, mood, or arrangement of qualities (Latin dis- 'apart' + ponere 'to place')

Put it together

Put it together: Predisposition combines pre- ('before') with disposition (dis- 'apart' + ponere 'to place') -- literally an arrangement 'placed' in someone beforehand, shaping how they're likely to act.

Use the root in a new word: disposition
